page: Hetzner Cloud ccx63 is a dedicated CPU server instance powered by the x86_64 AMD EPYC processor architecture. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs derived from 24 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. The system is provisioned with 188.0 GB of RAM, yielding approximately 3.91 GB of memory per core. Local storage is provided via a bundled 960 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance runs under a QEMU hypervisor. No complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core capabilities, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance scoring 73209.23 and a PassMark CPU score of 64305.59, both placing in the top 25%. The server demonstrates high efficiency in specialized tasks, achieving strong ratings in software compilation with Clang (46060.0), ray tracing (59291.0), and database operations (22243.57). Cryptographic and mathematical operations are supported by hardware-accelerated instructions including AES, SHA_NI, and AVX, reflected in a strong PassMark encryption score of 58566.64. Memory bandwidth performance remains in the average tier, with uncached read speeds of 148.56 GB/sec and write speeds of 80.13 GB/sec.

Given its dedicated resource allocation and balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the ccx63 offers high resource density and predictable performance without the noisy-neighbor risks of shared-core instances. This makes it highly cost-efficient for CPU-intensive, sustained workloads. It is highly suited for multi-threaded applications, database hosting, Redis deployments (achieving 62.09 million operations per second in SET benchmarks), software development pipelines, and medium-scale LLM inference tasks, where it achieves 28.13 tokens per second on 7B models.
